# rd02-02-integrated-estimates
if (recompute) {
  # Integrate each candidate over ALL of its independent conditional random
  # intercepts. Zero and dispersion specifications are identical across models.
  eligible <- comparison$model_id[comparison$convergence == 0 & comparison$pd_hessian]
  estimates <- bind_rows(lapply(eligible, function(id) integrated_means(models[[id]], id)))
  baseline <- filter(estimates, model_id == "thesis_site_species") |>
    select(treat, spp, baseline_mean = estimate, baseline_lcl = lcl, baseline_ucl = ucl)
  estimates <- left_join(estimates, baseline, by = c("treat", "spp")) |>
    mutate(mean_percent_change = 100 * (estimate / baseline_mean - 1),
           ci_width_ratio = (ucl - lcl) / (baseline_ucl - baseline_lcl))
  write.csv(estimates, file.path(out, "tables/rd02-integrated-model-comparison.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}

text:
Separate-species comparison
Redwood and tanoak may differ in their site and macro-plot variation as well as their mean responses. We’ll explore separate models that give each species its own variance components, then compare them with joint alternatives fitted to the same 128 redwood/tanoak rows. The fit, variance, and diagnostic tables below show what those assumptions imply for the two focal species.


Code
# rd02-03
if (recompute) {
  publication_root <- normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/")
  paths_common <- publication_paths(publication_root)
  suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(glmmTMB)
    library(DHARMa)
    library(dplyr)
    library(ggplot2)
  })
  input <- file.path(paths_common$input, "regeneration-measurements.rds")
  saved <- list(regen_pa = readRDS(input))
  d <- droplevels(subset(as.data.frame(saved$regen_pa), spp %in% c("rw", "to")))
  d$site <- factor(d$site)
  d$plot <- factor(d$plot)
  stopifnot(nrow(d) == 128L, !anyNA(d),
            nrow(distinct(d, site, treat, plot)) == 64L,
            all(count(d, site, treat, plot)$n == 2L))
  out <- file.path(paths_common$output, "regeneration/separate-species-comparison")
  for (directory in c("models", "tables", "diagnostics", "figures", "manifests")) {
    dir.create(file.path(out, directory), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  }
  spec <- list(
    rw_site_macro = list(species = "rw", formula = ba_ha ~ treat + (1 | site/treat)),
    to_site_macro = list(species = "to", formula = ba_ha ~ treat + (1 | site/treat)),
    joint_site_species_rwto = list(species = NULL, formula = ba_ha ~ treat*spp + (1 | site:spp)),
    joint_full_nested_rwto = list(species = NULL, formula = ba_ha ~ treat*spp + (1 | site/treat/plot)),
    joint_combined_rwto = list(species = NULL, formula = ba_ha ~ treat*spp + (1 | site/treat/plot) + (1 | site:spp))
  )
  models <- list()
  fit_records <- variance_records <- diagnostic_records <- list()
  seed <- 20261030L
  for (id in names(spec)) {
    item <- spec[[id]]
    model_data <- if (is.null(item$species)) d else droplevels(d[d$spp == item$species, ])
    if (!is.null(item$species)) {
      stopifnot(nrow(model_data) == 64L, all(count(model_data, site, treat, plot)$n == 1L))
    }
    message(if (isTRUE(params$refit)) "Fitting " else "Reading saved fit ", id)
    warnings <- character()
    m <- if (isTRUE(params$refit)) {
  withCallingHandlers(
      glmmTMB(item$formula, data = model_data, family = ziGamma(link = "log"),
              ziformula = if (is.null(item$species)) ~spp else ~1,
              dispformula = if (is.null(item$species)) ~spp else ~1,
              control = glmmTMBControl(optCtrl = list(iter.max = 10000, eval.max = 10000))),
      warning = function(w) {
        warnings <<- c(warnings, conditionMessage(w))
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      })
    } else {
      read_saved_model(file.path(out, "models", paste0(id, ".rds")), "RD02")
    }
    if (!isTRUE(params$refit)) {
      saved_register <- read.csv(file.path(out, "tables/rd02-species-fit-register.csv"))
      warnings <- stats::na.omit(saved_register$warnings[saved_register$model_id == id])
    }
    models[[id]] <- m
    if (!is.null(item$species)) {
      stopifnot(setequal(names(VarCorr(m)$cond), c("site", "treat:site")),
                !"plot" %in% names(model.frame(m)))
    }
    if (isTRUE(params$refit)) saveRDS(m, file.path(out, "models", paste0(id, ".rds")))
    vc <- VarCorr(m)$cond
    variance_records[[id]] <- bind_rows(lapply(names(vc), function(g) {
      variables <- strsplit(g, ":", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
      data.frame(model_id = id, group = g, n_groups = nrow(unique(model_data[variables])),
                 variance = vc[[g]][1, 1], sd = sqrt(vc[[g]][1, 1]))
    }))
    ll <- logLik(m)
    fit_records[[id]] <- data.frame(
      model_id = id, dataset = if (is.null(item$species)) "RW+TO" else toupper(item$species),
      n = nobs(m), n_zero = sum(model_data$ba_ha == 0), k = attr(ll, "df"),
      log_likelihood = as.numeric(ll), AIC = AIC(m), convergence = m$fit$convergence,
      pd_hessian = m$sdr$pdHess, max_abs_gradient = max(abs(m$sdr$gradient.fixed)),
      warnings = paste(unique(warnings), collapse = " | "))
    sim <- publication_simulate_residuals(m, n = 1000, seed = seed, refit = FALSE, plot = FALSE)
    tests <- list(uniformity = testUniformity, dispersion = testDispersion,
                  outliers = testOutliers, zero_inflation = testZeroInflation)
    diagnostic_records[[id]] <- bind_rows(lapply(names(tests), function(test) {
      result <- tests[[test]](sim, plot = FALSE)
      data.frame(model_id = id, test = test, statistic = unname(result$statistic)[1],
                 p_value = result$p.value)
    }))
    png(file.path(out, "diagnostics", paste0(id, "-dharma.png")),
        width = 1800, height = 1000, res = 160)
    plot(sim)
    dev.off()
    png(file.path(out, "diagnostics", paste0(id, "-by-treatment.png")),
        width = 1200, height = 1000, res = 160)
    plotResiduals(sim, form = model_data$treat)
    dev.off()
  }
  fit_table <- bind_rows(fit_records)
  variances <- bind_rows(variance_records)
  diagnostics <- bind_rows(diagnostic_records)
  stopifnot(all(fit_table$convergence == 0), all(fit_table$pd_hessian))
  write.csv(fit_table, file.path(out, "tables/rd02-species-fit-register.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(variances, file.path(out, "tables/rd02-species-variance-components.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(diagnostics, file.path(out, "tables/rd02-species-dharma-tests.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}

  publication_table(read.csv("outputs/regeneration/separate-species-comparison/tables/rd02-species-dharma-tests.csv"))
)










To assess relative support for separate versus joint fits, we need likelihoods for the same observations. We’ll add the two independent species log likelihoods and parameter counts to represent the separate pair in the AIC table below. That pair can be compared with the joint 128-row fits; individual-species AICs and the earlier 256-row AICs answer different comparisons.


Code
# rd02-03-paired-aic
if (recompute) {
  # A pair of independent species models has a product likelihood on these same
  # 128 rows; sum log likelihoods AND parameter counts. Do not compare the 64-row
  # individual AICs, or this paired AIC, against the earlier 256-row model AICs.
  separate <- filter(fit_table, dataset != "RW+TO")
  stopifnot(nrow(separate) == 2L, all(separate$k == 8L))
  joint <- filter(fit_table, dataset == "RW+TO")
  comparison <- bind_rows(
    transmute(joint, model_id, n, k, log_likelihood, AIC),
    data.frame(model_id = "separate_site_macro_pair", n = sum(separate$n),
      k = sum(separate$k), log_likelihood = sum(separate$log_likelihood), AIC = sum(separate$AIC))
  ) |>
    mutate(delta_AIC = AIC - min(AIC))
  stopifnot(all(comparison$n == 128L),
            max(abs(comparison$AIC - (-2 * comparison$log_likelihood + 2 * comparison$k))) < 1e-8)
  write.csv(comparison, file.path(out, "tables/rd02-rwto-aic-comparison.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}

Before interpreting the separate-species estimates, we’ll check whether a second optimizer reaches the same objective from random-effect SDs of 0.3. Agreement and convergence in the table below help us judge the numerical stability of these fits, especially where a variance component approaches zero.

  optimizer_checks <- bind_rows(lapply(c("rw_site_macro", "to_site_macro"), function(id) {
    model_data <- droplevels(d[d$spp == spec[[id]]$species, ])
    m <- models[[id]]
    warnings <- character()
    check <- if (isTRUE(params$refit)) {
  withCallingHandlers(glmmTMB(spec[[id]]$formula, data = model_data,
      family = ziGamma(link = "log"), ziformula = ~1, dispformula = ~1,

                              optCtrl = list(maxit = 10000, reltol = 1e-10))),
      warning = function(w) {
        warnings <<- c(warnings, conditionMessage(w))
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      })
    } else {
      read_saved_model(file.path(out, "models", paste0(id, "-bfgs.rds")), "RD02")
    }
    difference <- check$fit$objective - m$fit$objective
    if (isTRUE(params$refit)) saveRDS(check, file.path(out, "models", paste0(id, "-bfgs.rds")))
    stopifnot(check$fit$convergence == 0, abs(difference) < 1e-4)
    data.frame(model_id = id, convergence = check$fit$convergence, pd_hessian = check$sdr$pdHess,
      objective_difference_from_nlminb = difference, warnings = paste(unique(warnings), collapse = " | "))
  }))
  write.csv(optimizer_checks, file.path(out, "tables/rd02-species-optimizer-checks.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}

We’ll now translate the eligible redwood/tanoak fits into the same integrated mean basal-area estimand. The estimate table gives treatment means and full-covariance intervals, allowing us to assess whether separating species changes the biological pattern or mainly its uncertainty.

    integrated_means(models[[id]], id, spec[[id]]$species)

title: RD02 - regeneration basal-area/density display
text:
Selected four-species models
The current publication approach treats each species category as a distinct biological response, with its own site and macro-plot variation. We’ll apply that choice to all four categories, including Douglas-fir and other species so the supporting estimates remain complete. The tables below record fit quality, variance components, residual diagnostics, and optimizer agreement for each model.


Code
# rd02-05
if (recompute) {
  publication_root <- normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/")
  paths_common <- publication_paths(publication_root)
  suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(glmmTMB); library(DHARMa); library(dplyr); library(ggplot2)})
  input <- file.path(paths_common$input, "regeneration-measurements.rds")
  saved <- list(regen_pa = readRDS(input))
  d <- as.data.frame(saved$regen_pa)
  d$site <- factor(d$site)
  d$plot <- factor(d$plot)
  species_order <- c("rw", "to", "df", "other")
  species_labels <- c(rw = "Redwood", to = "Tanoak", df = "Douglas-fir", other = "Other species")
  stopifnot(nrow(d) == 256L, !anyNA(d), setequal(unique(d$spp), species_order))
  out <- file.path(paths_common$output, "regeneration/selected-species-models")
  for (directory in c("models", "tables", "diagnostics", "figures", "manifests")) {
    dir.create(file.path(out, directory), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  }
  models <- list()
  fit_records <- variance_records <- diagnostic_records <- optimizer_records <- list()
  seed <- 20261030L
  for (sp in species_order) {
    message(if (isTRUE(params$refit)) "Fitting species category: " else "Reading saved species fit: ", sp)
    data_sp <- droplevels(d[d$spp == sp, ])
    stopifnot(nrow(data_sp) == 64L, n_distinct(data_sp$site) == 4L,
              nrow(distinct(data_sp, site, treat)) == 16L,
              all(count(data_sp, site, treat, plot)$n == 1L))
    warnings <- character()
    m <- if (isTRUE(params$refit)) {
  withCallingHandlers(glmmTMB(
      ba_ha ~ treat + (1 | site/treat), data = data_sp,
      family = ziGamma(link = "log"), ziformula = ~1, dispformula = ~1,
      control = glmmTMBControl(optCtrl = list(iter.max = 10000, eval.max = 10000))),
      warning = function(w) { warnings <<- c(warnings, conditionMessage(w)); invokeRestart("muffleWarning") })
    } else {
      read_saved_model(file.path(out, "models", paste0(sp, "_site_macro.rds")), "RD02")
    }
    stopifnot(m$fit$convergence == 0, m$sdr$pdHess,
              setequal(names(VarCorr(m)$cond), c("site", "treat:site")),
              !"plot" %in% names(model.frame(m)))
    if (!isTRUE(params$refit)) {
      saved_register <- read.csv(file.path(out, "tables/rd02-selected-species-fit-register.csv"))
      warnings <- stats::na.omit(saved_register$warnings[saved_register$spp == sp])
    }
    models[[sp]] <- m
    if (isTRUE(params$refit)) saveRDS(m, file.path(out, "models", paste0(sp, "_site_macro.rds")))
    ll <- logLik(m)
    fit_records[[sp]] <- data.frame(spp = sp, species = species_labels[sp], model_id = paste0(sp, "_site_macro"),
      n = nobs(m), n_zero = sum(data_sp$ba_ha == 0), k = attr(ll, "df"),
      log_likelihood = as.numeric(ll), AIC = AIC(m), convergence = m$fit$convergence,
      pd_hessian = m$sdr$pdHess, max_abs_gradient = max(abs(m$sdr$gradient.fixed)),
      warnings = paste(unique(warnings), collapse = " | "), row.names = NULL)
    variance_records[[sp]] <- bind_rows(lapply(names(VarCorr(m)$cond), function(g) {
      value <- VarCorr(m)$cond[[g]][1, 1]
      data.frame(spp = sp, group = g, n_groups = nrow(unique(data_sp[strsplit(g, ":", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]])),
                 variance = value, sd = sqrt(value))
    }))
    sim <- publication_simulate_residuals(m, n = 1000, seed = seed, refit = FALSE, plot = FALSE)
    tests <- list(uniformity = testUniformity, dispersion = testDispersion,
                  outliers = testOutliers, zero_inflation = testZeroInflation)
    diagnostic_records[[sp]] <- bind_rows(lapply(names(tests), function(test) {
      result <- tests[[test]](sim, plot = FALSE)
      data.frame(spp = sp, test = test, statistic = unname(result$statistic)[1], p_value = result$p.value)
    }))
    png(file.path(out, "diagnostics", paste0(sp, "-dharma.png")), width = 1800, height = 1000, res = 160)
    plot(sim)
    dev.off()
    png(file.path(out, "diagnostics", paste0(sp, "-by-treatment.png")), width = 1200, height = 1000, res = 160)
    plotResiduals(sim, form = data_sp$treat)
    dev.off()
    if (isTRUE(params$refit)) {
    check_warnings <- character()
    alternative <- withCallingHandlers(glmmTMB(
      ba_ha ~ treat + (1 | site/treat), data = data_sp,
      family = ziGamma(link = "log"), ziformula = ~1, dispformula = ~1,
      start = list(theta = rep(log(.3), 2)),
      control = glmmTMBControl(optimizer = optim, optArgs = list(method = "BFGS"),
                              optCtrl = list(maxit = 10000, reltol = 1e-10))),
      warning = function(w) { check_warnings <<- c(check_warnings, conditionMessage(w)); invokeRestart("muffleWarning") })
    saveRDS(alternative, file.path(out, "models", paste0(sp, "_site_macro-bfgs.rds")))
    objective_difference <- alternative$fit$objective - m$fit$objective
    stopifnot(alternative$fit$convergence == 0, abs(objective_difference) < 1e-4)
    optimizer_records[[sp]] <- data.frame(spp = sp, convergence = alternative$fit$convergence,
      pd_hessian = alternative$sdr$pdHess, objective_difference_from_nlminb = objective_difference,
      warnings = paste(unique(check_warnings), collapse = " | "))
    } else {
      saved_checks <- read.csv(file.path(out, "tables/rd02-selected-species-optimizer-checks.csv"))
      optimizer_records[[sp]] <- saved_checks[saved_checks$spp == sp, ]
    }
  }
  fit_table <- bind_rows(fit_records)
  variances <- bind_rows(variance_records)
  diagnostics <- bind_rows(diagnostic_records)
  optimizer_checks <- bind_rows(optimizer_records)
  stopifnot(all(fit_table$k == 8L), nrow(variances) == 8L, nrow(diagnostics) == 16L)

  write.csv(fit_table, file.path(out, "tables/rd02-selected-species-fit-register.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(variances, file.path(out, "tables/rd02-selected-species-variances.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(diagnostics, file.path(out, "tables/rd02-selected-species-diagnostics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(optimizer_checks, file.path(out, "tables/rd02-selected-species-optimizer-checks.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}

  publication_table(read.csv("outputs/regeneration/selected-species-models/tables/rd02-selected-species-diagnostics.csv")),
  publication_table(read.csv("outputs/regeneration/selected-species-models/tables/rd02-selected-species-optimizer-checks.csv"))

What basal area does each selected model imply for each overstory treatment? We’ll calculate all 16 means, including absence probabilities and integrating site and macro-plot variation. The table below gives the four-category results and their intervals; prediction, gradient, and quadrature checks accompany the calculation before we use it in the manuscript.


Code
# rd02-05-integrated-estimates

           interval_method = "95% log-scale delta method using full parameter covariance") |>

            all(estimates$lcl > 0), all(estimates$lcl <= estimates$estimate), all(estimates$ucl >= estimates$estimate))
  write.csv(estimates, file.path(out, "tables/rd02-selected-species-estimates.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(optimizer_checks, file.path(out, "tables/rd02-selected-species-optimizer-checks.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}

title: RD02 - regeneration basal-area/density display
text:
Assemble the sensitivity display
We’ve considered several model structures in separate steps. We’ll now bring their saved results together to see how much the regeneration interpretation depends on those choices. This first cell assembles fit statistics, preserving the fitting-data scope so AIC differences are calculated within comparable groups.


Code
# tbl-rd02-random-effects-fit
# tbl-rd02-random-effects-fit
if (recompute) {
  publication_root <- normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/")
  paths_common <- publication_paths(publication_root)
  suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr); library(ggplot2)})
  root <- file.path(paths_common$output, "regeneration")
  joint_dir <- file.path(root, "random-effects-comparison/tables")
  species_dir <- file.path(root, "separate-species-comparison/tables")
  selected_dir <- file.path(root, "selected-species-models/tables")
  inputs <- c(
    fit4 = file.path(joint_dir, "rd02-model-comparison.csv"),
    var4 = file.path(joint_dir, "rd02-random-effect-variances.csv"),
    diag4 = file.path(joint_dir, "rd02-dharma-tests.csv"),
    mean4 = file.path(joint_dir, "rd02-integrated-model-comparison.csv"),
    component2 = file.path(species_dir, "rd02-species-fit-register.csv"),
    fit2 = file.path(species_dir, "rd02-rwto-aic-comparison.csv"),
    var2 = file.path(species_dir, "rd02-species-variance-components.csv"),
    diag2 = file.path(species_dir, "rd02-species-dharma-tests.csv"),
    mean2 = file.path(species_dir, "rd02-species-integrated-estimates.csv"),
    selected_fit = file.path(selected_dir, "rd02-selected-species-fit-register.csv"),
    selected_var = file.path(selected_dir, "rd02-selected-species-variances.csv"),
    selected_diag = file.path(selected_dir, "rd02-selected-species-diagnostics.csv"),
    selected_mean = file.path(selected_dir, "rd02-selected-species-estimates.csv")
  )
  stopifnot(all(file.exists(inputs)))
  read_input <- function(key) read.csv(inputs[[key]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  fit4 <- read_input("fit4")
  component2 <- read_input("component2")
  fit2 <- read_input("fit2")
  selected_components <- read_input("selected_fit")
  meta <- data.frame(
    model_id = c("thesis_site_species", "full_nested", "nested_plus_site_species",
                 "joint_site_species_rwto", "joint_full_nested_rwto", "joint_combined_rwto",
                 "separate_site_macro_pair", "selected_separate_four_species"),
    fit_scope = c(rep("Four-species fits", 3), rep("RW/TO fits", 4), "Four-species fits"),
    model_label = c("Site x species", "Full nesting", "Nested + site x species",
                    "Site x species", "Full nesting", "Nested + site x species", "Separate: site + macro plot",
                    "Separate: site + macro plot")
  )
  annotate <- function(x) {
    x$component_model_id <- x$model_id
    x$model_id[x$model_id %in% c("rw_site_macro", "to_site_macro")] <- "separate_site_macro_pair"
    stopifnot(all(x$model_id %in% meta$model_id))
    left_join(x, meta, by = "model_id")
  }
  annotate_selected <- function(x) {
    x$component_model_id <- if ("model_id" %in% names(x)) x$model_id else paste0(x$spp, "_site_macro")
    x$model_id <- "selected_separate_four_species"
    left_join(x, meta, by = "model_id")
  }
  pair_components <- component2[component2$model_id %in% c("rw_site_macro", "to_site_macro"), ]
  fit2$convergence <- vapply(fit2$model_id, function(id) {
    rows <- if (id == "separate_site_macro_pair") pair_components else component2[component2$model_id == id, ]
    as.integer(any(rows$convergence != 0))
  }, integer(1))
  fit2$pd_hessian <- vapply(fit2$model_id, function(id) {
    rows <- if (id == "separate_site_macro_pair") pair_components else component2[component2$model_id == id, ]
    all(rows$pd_hessian)
  }, logical(1))
  fit <- bind_rows(
    select(fit4, model_id, n, k, log_likelihood, AIC, convergence, pd_hessian),
    select(fit2, model_id, n, k, log_likelihood, AIC, convergence, pd_hessian),
    data.frame(model_id = "selected_separate_four_species", n = sum(selected_components$n),
      k = sum(selected_components$k), log_likelihood = sum(selected_components$log_likelihood),
      AIC = sum(selected_components$AIC), convergence = as.integer(any(selected_components$convergence != 0)),
      pd_hessian = all(selected_components$pd_hessian))
  ) |>
    left_join(meta, by = "model_id") |>
    mutate(BIC = -2 * log_likelihood + log(n) * k,
           selected_primary = model_id == "selected_separate_four_species") |>
    group_by(fit_scope) |>
    mutate(delta_AIC_within_scope = AIC - min(AIC)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    arrange(match(model_id, c("thesis_site_species", "full_nested", "nested_plus_site_species",
                             "selected_separate_four_species", "joint_site_species_rwto",
                             "joint_full_nested_rwto", "joint_combined_rwto", "separate_site_macro_pair")))
  out <- file.path(root, "overall-sensitivity")
  for (directory in c("tables", "figures", "manifests")) {
    dir.create(file.path(out, directory), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  }
  write.csv(fit, file.path(out, "tables/rd02-overall-model-comparison.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}

rd02_cmp_fit <- read.csv("outputs/regeneration/overall-sensitivity/tables/rd02-overall-model-comparison.csv")
rd02_scope_label <- c(`Four-species fits` = "4 species (256)", `RW/TO fits` = "RW/TO (128)")
rd02_fit_table <- data.frame(
  Data = unname(rd02_scope_label[rd02_cmp_fit$fit_scope]),
  Model = ifelse(rd02_cmp_fit$selected_primary,
                 paste0(rd02_cmp_fit$model_label, " (selected)"), rd02_cmp_fit$model_label),
  Parameters = rd02_cmp_fit$k,
  AIC = rd02_cmp_fit$AIC,
  `Delta AIC` = rd02_cmp_fit$delta_AIC_within_scope,
  check.names = FALSE
)

Table 2: Sensitivity-model fit. Delta AIC is calculated within each dataset. Separate-species rows combine independent category likelihoods and parameter counts: 32 parameters for four categories, 16 for RW/TO. The selected primary analysis is marked. All component fits converged with positive-definite Hessians.










Next we’ll collect variance components, diagnostics, and means from those same fits. Together, these tables help us relate a change in interval width or mean to the underlying variance and residual evidence. Each estimate and interval endpoint is checked against its source, and individual model identities remain visible where separate species fits share one display label.


Code
# rd02-04-assemble-estimates
if (recompute) {
  variances <- bind_rows(annotate(read_input("var4")), annotate(read_input("var2")),
                        annotate_selected(read_input("selected_var"))) |>
    mutate(species_context = case_when(component_model_id == "rw_site_macro" ~ "Redwood",
                                       component_model_id == "to_site_macro" ~ "Tanoak",
                                       component_model_id == "df_site_macro" ~ "Douglas-fir",
                                       component_model_id == "other_site_macro" ~ "Other species",
                                       TRUE ~ "Shared variance"))
  diagnostics <- bind_rows(
    annotate(filter(read_input("diag4"), scope == "species_plot_rows")),
    annotate(mutate(read_input("diag2"), scope = "species_plot_rows")),
    annotate_selected(mutate(read_input("selected_diag"), scope = "species_plot_rows"))
  ) |>
    mutate(species_context = case_when(component_model_id == "rw_site_macro" ~ "Redwood",
                                       component_model_id == "to_site_macro" ~ "Tanoak",
                                       component_model_id == "df_site_macro" ~ "Douglas-fir",
                                       component_model_id == "other_site_macro" ~ "Other species",
                                       fit_scope == "Four-species fits" ~ "All four species",
                                       TRUE ~ "RW + TO"))
  mean_columns <- c("treat", "spp", "model_id", "estimate", "se", "lcl", "ucl",
                    "total_random_variance", "integration_multiplier")
  means <- bind_rows(annotate(select(read_input("mean4"), all_of(mean_columns))),
                     annotate(select(read_input("mean2"), all_of(mean_columns))),
                     annotate_selected(select(read_input("selected_mean"), all_of(mean_columns))))
  stopifnot(

    all(fit$n[fit$fit_scope == "Four-species fits"] == 256L),

title: RD02 - regeneration basal-area/density display
text:
Publication execution
Regeneration calculations use publication R 4.6.2 and publication/renv.lock. Committed thesis exports supply the data and historical references. Prediction, gradient, integration, optimizer, and diagnostic checks accompany the calculations above.


Selected-model source and diagnostics

The publication-only pipeline fits four separate categories from the saved regeneration data. All 16 means pass prediction, gradient, and integration checks; the RW/TO estimates reproduce the separate-species sensitivity fits. Thesis files and earlier joint-model artifacts remain unchanged.
Estimates, fit register, diagnostics, variance components, optimizer checks, generator, provenance, and figure PDF.



Analytical specifications and historical checks


Selected analysis and manuscript outputs
The selected manuscript analysis fits all four species categories separately: ba_ha ~ treat + (1 | site/treat), ziGamma(log), zero ~1, dispersion ~1. The selected-model calculation produces these outputs. Each category has 64 observations, four site groups, and 16 nested macro-plot groups. The plot-level random effect is omitted. Selection follows the user’s biological modeling decision rather than the minimum-AIC alternative.
Current outputs are under outputs/regeneration/selected-species-models/: 16 integrated means and full-covariance intervals, four fitted models, fit and variance registers, DHARMa plots/tests, optimizer checks, and provenance. All four models are checked against BFGS; all 16 means are verified using model predictions, numerical gradients, and quadrature. RW/TO means reproduce the same-species comparison. This task reads committed thesis exports and writes only publication outputs.


Historical joint-model reference
The historical reference calculation reads exported historical estimates and audit tables, then generates the reference display. The original mba replay, prediction, gradient, and quadrature checks execute in analysis/scripts/export-publication-inputs.R under thesis R and renv. Publication never loads analysis/regen_visualize.rda. The selected model is m5 from analysis/analysis/regen_visualize.qmd: zero-inflated Gamma, conditional log link, ba_ha ~ treat * spp + (1 | site:spp), zero and dispersion formulas ~spp. All four species classes remain in the fit. Only redwood and tanoak enter the main display. This is basal area per hectare, not stem density.
For species g and treatment t, the integrated expectation is (1 - p_zero[g]) * exp(X[t,g] beta + sigma_site:spp^2 / 2). There are no random effects in the zero component. Gamma dispersion needs no lognormal residual correction. Four site rows receive equal weights, but the integrated expectations coincide because site is not a fixed predictor. This is the same arithmetic-response estimand used for RD04, audited here for the regeneration model’s distinct structure.
The full sdr$cov.fixed covariance propagates uncertainty in conditional and zero coefficients and the log random-effect SD, including cross-covariances. Means use positive 95% log-scale delta-method intervals. Model-selection, measurement/aggregation, and model-structure uncertainty are not included. The retained site-by-species intercept does not explicitly model macro-plot clustering, unlike the fuel hierarchy. That design question remains open for scientific review; this script does not silently replace the thesis model.
Outputs in publication/outputs/regeneration/:

figures/rd02-regeneration-basal-area.png and .pdf: shared-scale historical display.
tables/rd02-basal-area-model-estimates.csv: all 16 species/treatment means.
tables/rd02-observed-basal-area-summary.csv: observed counts, zeros, and means.
inference-audit/: four-site grid and zero-effect/integrated comparison.
manifests/: model specification, review status, and session information.

The thesis export operation checks all 16 historical cells against predict() and marginaleffects for the zero-effect reference, and against marginaleffects::hypotheses() for integrated means and SEs. Independent numerical gradients and numerical quadrature verify the analytic derivatives and integration factor. Export integrity can be checked explicitly with the input checker. No significance arrows, inherited p-values, or claims based on CI overlap are generated. Refitted bootstrap intervals remain possible later modeling work.


Full nested design comparison
The joint comparison fits three models on the same 256 saved species/vegetation-plot rows:

Thesis: ba_ha ~ treat * spp + (1 | site:spp).
Full design: ba_ha ~ treat * spp + (1 | site/treat/plot).
Sensitivity: full design plus (1 | site:spp).

The full design expands to site, site:treatment (macro plot), and site:treatment:plot (vegetation plot) intercepts: 4, 16, and 64 groups. Plot/corner codes are reused and are not treated as globally unique IDs. All candidates use zero-inflated Gamma with conditional log link, the same treat*spp fixed effects, and ~spp zero and dispersion formulas. No random effects are added to the zero model. The sensitivity candidate distinguishes adding design clustering from removing species-specific site variation.
Outputs are in outputs/regeneration/random-effects-comparison/: ML fit/AIC/BIC/convergence records, variance components, row/grouped DHARMa tests and plots, integrated means and full-covariance delta-method intervals, optimizer and residual-tail sensitivity checks, and a model-comparison figure. The two primary covariance structures are not nested in one another; the comparison does not report an ordinary likelihood-ratio test. Lower AIC alone does not settle the scientific adequacy of a covariance structure.
The comparison checks refitted thesis likelihood against the saved fit, prediction matrices against predict(), and all integrated-mean gradients against numerical derivatives. It checks design-candidate optima using BFGS from initial random SDs of 0.3, alongside the main nlminb fits. Near-zero variance components are recorded rather than silently dropped. Their delta-method intervals are approximate near the boundary; no refitted bootstrap intervals are claimed.
DHARMa uses 1,000 unconditional simulations per model (seed 20261030), with recalculated residuals at site, macro-plot, and vegetation-plot levels. These checks are exploratory, not proof of independence; four sites provide little power at the site level. The baseline tail flag is checked again with 10,000 simulations and a different seed; flagged rows from both runs are retained. All observations remain in the fits.
The committed thesis exports are read-only inputs. Fitted models and simulations remain local RDS artifacts. The comparison is recorded in publication/sections/rd02-random-effects-review.qmd, included in the RD02 workflow card. It does not automatically replace the lead model.


Separate RW and TO models with site and macro-plot effects
03-compare-rd02-separate-species.R gives each focal species ba_ha ~ treat + (1 | site/treat), with ziGamma(log), zero ~1, and dispersion ~1. There are 64 observations, 4 sites, 16 macro plots, and 64 vegetation plots per species. Each fit estimates its own variance components. Within one species, site-by-species is simply site. The plot-level random intercept is omitted; each species has one observation per vegetation plot.
For a valid AIC comparison, all three joint alternatives are refitted on the same 128 RW/TO rows. The separate pair’s log likelihoods and parameter counts are summed under species independence. Neither individual-species AICs nor the paired AIC are compared with the earlier 256-row, four-species AICs. Cross-species covariance is not estimated by the independent fits.
Outputs are in outputs/regeneration/separate-species-comparison/: fit and variance registers, same-data AIC comparison, 1,000-simulation DHARMa checks and treatment plots, full-covariance integrated means and intervals, BFGS/start sensitivity checks, provenance, session, and a comparison figure. All 32 mean cells are checked using predict(), numerical gradients, and quadrature. Original inputs and lead figure/estimates are checksum protected. The workflow includes publication/sections/rd02-separate-species-review.qmd. The script does not replace the lead model or generate significance arrows.


Overall sensitivity figures and tables
04-assemble-rd02-sensitivity.R reads their generated CSVs without refitting models or recalculating inference. The overall collection includes the three four-species joint fits, three RW/TO joint refits, the separate site/macro-plot RW/TO pair, and the selected four-category separate models.
outputs/regeneration/overall-sensitivity/ contains a four-panel figure (fitting-data scopes in rows, species in columns), an eight-configuration fit table, all 28 variance-component rows, 48 row-level diagnostic tests, and 96 complete mean/interval cells (64 focal-species cells in the figure). The separate species share a figure label; component_model_id preserves their individual fits. AIC differences are calculated within each data scope, never across the 256-row and 128-row groups.
The assembler checks that every source estimate and interval limit is copied exactly, all configuration/treatment/species cells are present once, AIC matches its log likelihood and parameter count. The overall and focused species figures remain in the workflow with one fit comparison table. Full estimates, variance components, and diagnostics are downloads; duplicate rendered tables are omitted. Review prose summarizes treatment patterns, notable variance/interval differences, and diagnostic trends.

title: RT03 - fuel Results narrative
section: Fuel conditions before and after precommercial thinning
text:
Fuel conditions before and after precommercial thinning

Dead fuel loading
Fuel measurements ten years after harvest characterized conditions before and after precommercial thinning (PCT) across the four retention treatments (Figure 1). Following PCT, group selection (GS) and low-density dispersed retention (LD) showed the largest estimated increases in fine dead-fuel loads and reductions in woody standing vegetation. These treatments also had the highest post-PCT fine dead-fuel loads. Pre-PCT dead-fuel estimates suggested subtler, component-specific treatment patterns. Fuel loads are reported as model-estimated means, with 95% confidence intervals. Woody and herbaceous standing vegetation are reported separately, as are pre-PCT litter and duff. All loads and load differences below are in Mg ha-1.
Before PCT, estimated 1-hour fuel loads were highest in high-density aggregated retention (HA; 1.2) and lowest in GS (0.6), with LD and high-density dispersed (HD) retention intermediate. Estimated 10-hour loads ranged from 2.8 in HD to 3.8 in GS, and 100-hour loads from 9.0 to 11.5 in those same treatments. The 1,000-hour class had larger mean loads, ranging from 30.2 in LD to 49.6 (95% CI 25.9 to 95.0) in GS. Uncertainty was substantial for this coarse-wood component across treatments.
The separated forest-floor components showed different treatment patterns. Pre-PCT litter estimates ranged from 12.6 in LD to 18.4 in GS; HA and HD were intermediate. Duff estimates were lowest in HA, at 19.3 (95% CI 14.5 to 25.8), and highest in HD, at 35.5 (95% CI 26.6 to 47.4), with GS and LD both near 28–29. These are model-derived forest-floor loads based on the estimated litter-depth boundary. Post-PCT litter and duff were not estimated because the forest-floor boundary could not be distinguished reliably in the presence of slash and suspended foliage.
After PCT, estimated 1-hour loads were about 2.4–2.7 in GS, LD, and HD, and 1.4 in HA. The 10-hour estimates were ordered GS (9.6), LD (5.9), HA (4.1), and HD (3.3). The 100-hour estimates followed the same order, from 19.6 (95% CI 11.8 to 32.8) in GS to 7.5 (95% CI 4.6 to 12.2) in HD. Post-PCT 1,000-hour means ranged from 25.2 in HA to 53.9 in GS, with wide confidence intervals. These rankings describe estimated loads; they do not establish pairwise treatment differences. title: Regeneration and fuel loading with varying overstory retention in redwood stands
text:
Forest managers using retention forestry need information on regeneration and fuel development to design productive stands in fire-adapted ecosystems. We analyzed 10-year remeasurement data from the Redwood Multiaged Experiment in Jackson Demonstration State Forest, California. The experiment compared group selection, aggregated retention, and low- and high-density dispersed retention treatments and measured regeneration, sprout growth, and surface fuel loading.
Redwood regeneration responded strongly to increasing canopy openness, whereas tanoak responses were more modest. Sprout-height findings will remain part of the main regeneration evidence. Fuel measurements describe conditions before and after precommercial thinning, including the PCT-associated contrast. The manuscript will evaluate how overstory retention affects regeneration while presenting fuel components in a form useful for integrated silviculture, fuels, and fire management.

title: Regeneration and fuel loading with varying overstory retention in redwood stands
text:
Study area and design
The experiment is located in the Jackson Demonstration State Forest in coastal northern California. Four harvest treatments were replicated at four sites in 2012: group selection (GS), high-density dispersed retention (HD), high-density aggregated retention (HA), and low-density dispersed retention (LD). The retained-overstory treatments targeted post-harvest relative densities of 13% or 21%; group selection created a 1-ha opening with a lightly thinned buffer. These treatments were designed to examine alternative pathways for developing multiaged redwood stands (Berrill & O’Hara, 2009; Reineke, 1933).
Ten years after harvest, regeneration plots and fuel transects were established within each 0.2-ha treatment macro plot. Regeneration measurements characterized redwood, tanoak, and Douglas-fir; fuel transects characterized dead surface fuels and live vegetation. The plots were remeasured after precommercial thinning, which released selected conifers from competing trees and shrubs.

title: Regeneration and fuel loading with varying overstory retention in redwood stands
text:
Analysis
Detailed sampling procedures, model diagnostics, and sensitivity analyses will be retained as supplementary material.

Regeneration basal area
Basal area was modeled separately for redwood, tanoak, Douglas-fir, and other species using zero-inflated Gamma mixed models with a conditional log link. Treatment was a fixed effect; site and macro plot nested within site were random intercepts. Each species category had its own intercept-only zero and dispersion components. Each model used 64 vegetation-plot observations from four sites and 16 macro plots. Arithmetic mean basal area included modeled zeros and integrated over both fitted Gaussian random-intercept distributions. Confidence intervals for the means were calculated using the log-scale delta method with the full parameter covariance, including random-effect variance uncertainty. Redwood and tanoak estimates are displayed in the Results; estimates for all four categories are reported in the supplement.


Fuel loads and PCT contrast
Reported values are model-based arithmetic mean loads, including modeled zeros and integrating over fitted random effects, with equal weights for the four study-site contexts.
These estimates provide model-based reference means for comparable forest conditions; 95% confidence intervals were calculated using the delta method with the full parameter covariance, including uncertainty in random-effect variances. Mean woody standing-vegetation reduction was estimated as the pre-PCT minus post-PCT contrast from the matched repeated-phase model, with its joint covariance, and interpreted as a potential surface-fuel contribution.

title: Introduction
text:
Introduction
Developing and maintaining multiaged stand structures requires silvicultural systems that create and sustain cohorts of different ages within the same stand (O’Hara, 1998; Schütz, 2002). Retention systems can retain a range of tree densities in dispersed or aggregated patterns and can be used to maintain multiaged stands or transform formerly even-aged stands (Mitchell & Beese, 2002).
Coast redwood (Sequoia sempervirens) is well suited to this objective because it regenerates reliably by stump sprouting and can grow beneath a retained overstory. Its response to light is nevertheless important: reduced access to light can limit sprout vigor and persistence (Berrill et al., 2018; Muma et al., 2022; O’Hara et al., 2007). Tanoak (Notholithocarpus densiflorus) is also shade tolerant and a vigorous resprouter, making its response relevant to both stand development and management of competing vegetation (Berrill et al., 2021; O’Hara et al., 2017).
Silvicultural decisions that promote regeneration also influence the fuel conditions in which later management and fire occur. This paper therefore examines regeneration under varying overstory retention and describes surface fuel conditions before and after precommercial thinning as reference information for integrated silvicultural, fuels, fire, and potential modeling applications.
We use 10-year measurements from the Redwood Multiaged Experiment to evaluate regeneration responses among retention treatments and to report fuel conditions before and after precommercial thinning, including their PCT-associated contrast. Redwood and tanoak provide the primary regeneration focus, with other species retained as descriptive context where useful. Fuel components will be presented in a publication-specific form after their analytical specification is reviewed.

title: RD04 - fuel phase and PCT display
text:
Audit prediction and uncertainty
Before using the estimates, we’ll compare the analytic and marginaleffects calculations for 60 zero-effect references, 60 integrated means, and four woody contrasts, holding the F01 fits and prediction grids fixed. The check requires absolute mean differences below \(10^{-6}\) Mg/ha and SE differences divided by \(\max(1, \mathrm{SE}_{\mathrm{analytic}})\) below \(10^{-4}\). The summary records the largest discrepancies across all cells; subsequent tables use only the analytic route.


Inspect the calculation and method-agreement summary



Code
# rd04-07-method-agreement
if (recompute) {
  publication_root <- normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/")
  paths_common <- publication_paths(publication_root)
  suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(dplyr)
    library(glmmTMB)
    library(marginaleffects)
    library(readr)
    library(tidyr)
  })
  models_dir <- file.path(publication_root, "outputs", "fuel", "models")
  audit_dir <- file.path(paths_common$output, "fuel/inference-audit")
  dir.create(audit_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  spec <- bind_rows(
    filter(rd04_spec, !is.na(phase)),
    mutate(filter(rd04_spec, component == "Woody vegetation"), phase = "prepct"),
    mutate(filter(rd04_spec, component == "Woody vegetation"), phase = "postpct")
  ) |>
    mutate(
      component = sub(" fuel$", "", component),
      component = sub(" (pre-PCT only)", "", component, fixed = TRUE)
    )
  # Include the signed alternative used in the later estimand comparison.
  spec <- bind_rows(
    spec,
    transmute(
      filter(selection, response == "woody standing-vegetation reduction"),
      model_id = provisional_aic_leader,
      component = "Woody difference",
      phase = NA_character_
    )
  )
  agreement_row <- function(target, estimate, se, comparison) {
    tibble(
      target = target,
      cells = length(estimate),
      max_mean_difference = max(abs(estimate - comparison$estimate)),
      max_scaled_se_difference = max(abs(se - comparison$std.error) / pmax(1, se))
    )
  }
  agreement <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(spec))) {
    item <- spec[i, ]
    model <- read_saved_model(
      file.path(models_dir, paste0(item$model_id, ".rds")), "F01"
    )
    grid <- reference_grid(model, if (is.na(item$phase)) NULL else item$phase)
    reference <- custom_reference(model, grid)
    me <- as.data.frame(avg_predictions(
      model, newdata = grid, type = "response",
      by = intersect(c("treatment", "phase"), names(grid)),
      re.form = NA, allow.new.levels = TRUE
    ))
    me <- me[match(as.character(reference$treatment), as.character(me$treatment)), ]
    s <- integration_setup(model, grid)
    integrated <- custom_integrated(s)
    agreement[[length(agreement) + 1L]] <- agreement_row(
      "Zero-effect references", reference$estimate, reference$std.error, me
    )
    agreement[[length(agreement) + 1L]] <- agreement_row(
      "Integrated means", integrated$estimate, integrated$se,
      as.data.frame(marginaleffects_integrated(s))
    )
  }
  woody <- read_saved_model(
    file.path(models_dir, paste0(rd04_spec$model_id[
      rd04_spec$component == "Woody vegetation"
    ], ".rds")), "F01"
  )
  s <- woody_change_setup(integration_setup(woody, reference_grid(woody)))
  change <- custom_integrated(s)
  agreement[[length(agreement) + 1L]] <- agreement_row(
    "Woody pre-minus-post contrasts", change$estimate, change$se,
    as.data.frame(marginaleffects_integrated(s))
  )
  method_agreement <- bind_rows(agreement) |>
    group_by(target) |>
    summarise(
      cells = sum(cells),
      max_mean_difference = max(max_mean_difference),
      max_scaled_se_difference = max(max_scaled_se_difference),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      mean_tolerance = 1e-6,
      scaled_se_tolerance = 1e-4,
      passed = max_mean_difference < mean_tolerance &
        max_scaled_se_difference < scaled_se_tolerance
    )
  stopifnot(all(method_agreement$passed))
  write_csv(method_agreement, file.path(audit_dir, "rd04-method-agreement.csv"))
}
method_agreement <- read.csv("outputs/fuel/inference-audit/rd04-method-agreement.csv")
stopifnot(all(method_agreement$passed))
publication_table(method_agreement)







The analytic and marginaleffects calculations agree within both tolerances for all 124 checked targets. Subsequent tables use the analytic route. Agreement checks the implementation, not model adequacy. The estimand audit below also checks integration against numerical quadrature and matrix predictions against predict.glmmTMB().
Next we’ll examine how the prediction target changes the estimated loads.


Inspect prediction targets and model structures

In the first table, model_id, component, phase, and treatment identify the fit and prediction target; n_sites counts the equally weighted sites. The remaining headings distinguish three ways to summarize the fitted model:

reference_estimate gives mean predictions with random effects set to zero; reference_se gives their covariance-aware standard errors.
fitted_group_site_balanced_mean averages predictions using the sampled groups’ fitted random effects, first within sites and then equally across sites.
random_intercept_variance sums the fitted intercept variances on the link scale; integration_multiplier is the resulting mean adjustment, \(\exp(v/2)\) for log-link models and 1 for the identity-link difference model.
integrated_estimate averages over the fitted random-effect distribution. integrated_se includes uncertainty in the estimated random-effect variances, and integrated_lcl/integrated_ucl bound the 95% confidence interval for the mean. Estimates, standard errors, and limits are in Mg/ha.

The second table records model formulas: conditional describes fuel load, zero the modeled probability of a structural zero, and dispersion the residual dispersion structure.


Code
# rd04-07-audit-rd04-inference
if (recompute) {
  audit <- list()
  structures <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(spec))) {
    item <- spec[i, ]
    message("Auditing ", item$model_id, " ", item$phase)
    model <- read_saved_model(
      file.path(models_dir, paste0(item$model_id, ".rds")),
      "F01"
    )
    phase_arg <- if (is.na(item$phase)) NULL else item$phase
    grid <- reference_grid(model, phase_arg)
    avg <- averaging_matrix(grid)
    reference <- custom_reference(model, grid)
    s <- integration_setup(model, grid)
    integrated <- custom_integrated(s)
    # Verify integration at a point using numerical quadrature, independently of
    # the closed-form exp(v/2) calculation (including near-zero variances).
    if (s$link == "log") {
      quadrature <- integrate(
        function(z) exp(sqrt(s$variance) * z) * dnorm(z),
        lower = -12,
        upper = 12,
        rel.tol = 1e-9
      )$value
      stopifnot(abs(quadrature - exp(s$variance / 2)) < 1e-7)
    }
    # Check matrix construction against the model's own predict implementation.
    row0 <- if (s$link == "log") {
      exp(drop(s$X %*% s$par[s$ib]))
    } else {
      drop(s$X %*% s$par[s$ib])
    }
    if (length(s$iz)) {
      row0 <- row0 * (1 - plogis(drop(s$Z %*% s$par[s$iz])))
    }
    stopifnot(
      max(abs(row0 - predict(model, grid, type = "response", re.form = NA))) <
        1e-6
    )
    # Average ALL observed rows within site, then equally across sites; retaining
    # only one corner/transect per site would give an arbitrary conditional mean.
    observed <- model$frame
    if (!is.null(phase_arg) && "phase" %in% names(observed)) {
      observed <- filter(observed, .data$phase == .env$phase_arg)
    }
    conditional <- observed |>
      mutate(
        predicted = as.numeric(predict(
          model,
          observed,
          type = "response",
          re.form = NULL
        ))
      ) |>
      group_by(across(all_of(intersect(
        c("site", "treatment", "phase"),
        names(observed)
      )))) |>
      summarise(predicted = mean(predicted), .groups = "drop") |>
      group_by(across(all_of(intersect(
        c("treatment", "phase"),
        names(observed)
      )))) |>
      summarise(predicted = mean(predicted), .groups = "drop")
    fitted_groups <- conditional$predicted[match(
      as.character(reference$treatment),
      as.character(conditional$treatment)
    )]
    # Marginal mean intervals: log-delta intervals stay positive without truncation;
    # the signed identity-link difference uses ordinary response-scale intervals.
    lcl <- if (s$link == "log") {
      integrated$estimate *
        exp(-qnorm(.975) * integrated$se / integrated$estimate)
    } else {
      integrated$estimate - qnorm(.975) * integrated$se
    }
    ucl <- if (s$link == "log") {
      integrated$estimate *
        exp(qnorm(.975) * integrated$se / integrated$estimate)
    } else {
      integrated$estimate + qnorm(.975) * integrated$se
    }
    # Keep reference, fitted-group, and integrated targets side by side. The
    # fitted-group mean describes sampled groups; it is not the integrated target.
    audit[[i]] <- tibble(
      model_id = item$model_id,
      component = item$component,
      phase = item$phase,
      treatment = as.character(reference$treatment),
      n_sites = rowSums(avg$A > 0),
      reference_estimate = reference$estimate,
      reference_se = reference$std.error,
      fitted_group_site_balanced_mean = fitted_groups,
      random_intercept_variance = s$variance,
      integration_multiplier = if (s$link == "log") exp(s$variance / 2) else 1,
      integrated_estimate = integrated$estimate,
      integrated_se = integrated$se,
      integrated_lcl = lcl,
      integrated_ucl = ucl
    )
    structures[[i]] <- tibble(
      model_id = item$model_id,
      phase = item$phase,
      conditional = deparse1(formula(model)),
      zero = deparse1(formula(model, component = "zi")),
      dispersion = deparse1(formula(model, component = "disp"))
    )
  }
  audit <- bind_rows(audit)
  write_csv(audit, file.path(audit_dir, "rd04-estimand-comparison.csv"))
  structure_path <- file.path(audit_dir, "model-structures.csv")
  structure_table <- as.data.frame(bind_rows(structures))
  write_csv(structure_table, structure_path)
}

htmltools::tagList(
  publication_table(read.csv(
    "outputs/fuel/inference-audit/rd04-estimand-comparison.csv"
  )),
  publication_table(read.csv(
    "outputs/fuel/inference-audit/model-structures.csv"
  ))
)









Integration multiplies herbaceous means by about 2.0–2.3, raises woody vegetation means by 33%, and changes duff by only 0.3%. The prediction target matters most where fitted random-effect variation is larger.
We’ll compare joint-model woody change with observed differences and the direct Student-t model to examine the consequences of the change-model choice.


Inspect observed, joint-model, and Student-t woody changes



Code
# rd04-07-woody-contrast
if (recompute) {
  # A coherent mean change uses the same repeated-phase model on both sides and
  # its cross-phase covariance. Compare with the independently fitted t model.
  woody <- read_saved_model(
    file.path(
      models_dir,
      paste0(spec$model_id[spec$component == "Woody vegetation"][1], ".rds")
    ),
    "F01"
  )
  s <- integration_setup(woody, reference_grid(woody))
  s <- woody_change_setup(s)
  treatments <- as.character(s$avg$labels$treatment)
  change <- custom_integrated(s)
  # Descriptive observed change uses the same equal-site weighting as the target.
  # It provides context, rather than replacing the joint model's mean contrast.
  observed <- woody$frame |>
    group_by(treatment, phase, site) |>
    summarise(load = mean(load_mgha), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(treatment, phase) |>
    summarise(load = mean(load), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = phase, values_from = load) |>
    mutate(observed_difference = prepct - postpct)
  # Signed changes can cross zero, so use response-scale Wald limits with the
  # joint-model SE; join the separate t-model estimate only for comparison.
  phase_change <- tibble(
    treatment = treatments,
    phase_model_difference = change$estimate,
    se = change$se,
    lcl = change$estimate - qnorm(.975) * change$se,
    ucl = change$estimate + qnorm(.975) * change$se
  ) |>
    left_join(
      select(observed, treatment, observed_difference),
      by = "treatment"
    ) |>
    left_join(
      select(
        filter(audit, component == "Woody difference"),
        treatment,
        separate_t_model_difference = integrated_estimate
      ),
      by = "treatment"
    )
  write_csv(
    phase_change,
    file.path(audit_dir, "woody-mean-change-comparison.csv")
  )
}

publication_table(read.csv(
  "outputs/fuel/inference-audit/woody-mean-change-comparison.csv"
))
